--- GAP-008 OPEN 
 source_locators.doi IS SHUFFLED RELATIVE TO title/authors/pub_year ACROSS THE PRE-RESET MIGRATION, AND IT BREAKS R9 IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Found by the write path, not by a check: db.py add-source refused REF-00999 (Rouvier 2022) because DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0269657 is 'already filed as REF-00037', and refused Kim 2014's 10.1016/j.ergon.2014.07.001 as 'already filed as REF-00030'. BOTH REFUSALS ARE FALSE. On each row the doi+issn pair is internally consistent and correct for the NEW source, while title/authors/pub_year describe a DIFFERENT work: REF-00037 carries the PLoS One DOI and ISSN 1932-6203 under the title 'Inclusive Housing Design Guide' (Runnalls & Walker 2024, which embeds its OWN different DOI 10.4324/9781003564164 inside the title string); REF-00030 carries the Int J Industrial Ergonomics DOI and ISSN 0169-8141 under a speech-intelligibility/classroom-acoustics title (Murgia et al.). CONSEQUENCE, and the second half is the worse one: R9 dedup fires FALSE COLLISIONS that block correct admissions (2 of 5 candidate DOIs in this batch), and by the same shuffle it must also FALSE-CLEAR real duplicates whose DOI landed on some other row -- silently failing the check R9 exists to be. SCALE: derive it, never quote it. The exposed population is rows where doi is not null; the subset whose title embeds a DIFFERENT doi than the doi column is the ONLY mechanically detectable signature, so that count is a FLOOR, not an estimate -- rows whose title embeds no DOI are undetectable by it. Nearly all exposed rows carry recovered_from='corpus-pre-reset-2026-08-06'. REPAIR IS BLOCKED ON A WRITER: db.py has no command that can set source_locators.doi or .title, and correct-source operates on evidence_sources only. source_locators_integrity has been reporting this at ADVISORY level as a title-quality issue; it is actually a DOI-reliability defect that breaks a blocking gate, and the framing understated it.

--- GAP-016 OPEN 
 READ VREDENBURGH ET AL. 2009 (REF-01002) IN FULL. IT IS THE FIRST ANCHORING-TIER STATED MAXIMUM THIS PARAMETER HAS HAD, AND IT IS HELD AT SKIM GRADE. The TRID/TRB record and its verbatim abstract were retrieved and persisted this batch (HTTP 200, 50825 bytes) and give: Results suggest that for a transit distance of up to 20 feet, a ramp should not exceed a maximum cross slope of 5% or a maximum running slope of 7%. THE ARTICLE ITSELF WAS NOT RETRIEVED. Journal of Architectural and Planning Research 26(2):145-158, ISSN 0738-0895, NO DOI -- which is why six batches of DOI-keyed searching never met it and why it sat unread inside REF-00977 reference list. WHAT THE FULL READ MUST SETTLE, none of which the abstract answers: (1) the participant count and composition -- the record says users of manual AND motorised wheelchairs and states no n, so the population match is graded PARTIAL on an unknown denominator; (2) the slope set actually tested, since 7% may be a recommendation or merely the highest slope at which perceived effort did not degrade, and those are different claims; (3) whether the 20-foot transit distance is a tested bound or an assumption; (4) whether disabled people shaped the study beyond serving as subjects, which under D-0178 is the difference between T1 and Co-1. ON RESOLUTION: promote extraction 45 from skim/preliminary, resolve determination gate 1, and re-determine parameter 3 x MOB -- or record that the abstract overstated. UNTIL THEN THE FIGURE DOES NOT MOVE. Specification 8 stands at 5% and is SAFE rather than correct: 7% is LOOSER, the parameter direction is lower_is_better, so the standing value errs conservative while its tier_basis (T4-6-only-threshold, rests_on_proxy_inference=1) describes the wrong evidence. Batch 15 refused to claim Co-1 for REF-01001 on an ambiguous abstract and the full text vindicated the refusal; this is the same discipline one column along. TRID also lists the publisher as Elsevier Science, which is wrong for this journal -- do not propagate it; the publisher field was left unwritten for that reason.

--- GAP-023 OPEN 
 GAP-019 RESOLVED 2026-09-18, AND HALF OF WHAT IT CLAIMED WAS AN INSTRUMENTATION ERROR OF MINE THAT MUST BE RETRACTED. THE REAL DEFECT, FIXED: the gate cap at assess_cell.py (state stated + any binding gate -> provisional) downgraded the cell WITHOUT supplying the confidence flag that provisional requires, so EvidenceStateRecord refused it as an uncaught pydantic traceback and nothing was written. The anchored branch sets state=stated and leaves conf None, which is correct for a stated cell; the cap then moved the state and left conf behind it. determination_gates held ZERO rows until batch 16 raised gate 1, so this branch had NEVER EXECUTED in the engine life -- the defect was created by the first gate ever raised, which was mine. NOT A DOCTRINE QUESTION, which is what GAP-019 claimed it was: the fix is descriptive, present is the anchoring basis the cell already has and absent names the gate that caps it, both read off state the function already holds. A second bug rode along -- the flag read the gate dict key detail where derivation_handshake names it why, so the first version named the gate and then said nothing about it. WHAT IS RETRACTED: GAP-019 second half asserted that a single T1 claim DISPLACED the entire regulatory stratum, citing governing and supporting both None. THAT IS FALSE AND THE CAUSE WAS MY PROBE, NOT THE ENGINE. I printed det.get(governing); the key is governing_refs, and it reads [REF-01002] correctly. Re-measured: governing_refs=[REF-01002], tier_basis=T1, supporting_refs=[]. The regulatory sources dropping OUT of the governing set once an anchor exists is the RATIFIED LADDER working -- T4-T6 are walled off from full-strength anchoring -- not a defect and not displacement. The claim reached GAP-019, the session record, the attestation and the PR body; all four are corrected. CLAUDE.md rule 7a applies to a figure read off a dict key as much as to one typed by hand.

--- GAP-025 OPEN 
 BATCH 17 MINING ASSIGNMENT — owner instruction 2026-09-18, answering GAP-022: "then assign the mining for the next batch". THE MECHANISM FOR "runs eventually" IS ASSIGNMENT, NOT AN AGEING METRIC. GAP-022 named the missing half of the 2026-09-18 ruling (deferred is okay so long as it runs eventually) and proposed building an age or backlog measure. The owner answered by assigning the work instead, which is the cheaper and more honest instrument: a deferral runs because a batch is told to run it, not because a counter goes red. DERIVE THE BACKLOG, NEVER QUOTE IT -- select slug, global_ref_id, deferred_reason from citation_mining where deferred_reason is not null; measured 2026-09-18 at ten rows, all on accessible-circulation-geometry. BATCH 17 TAKES THESE, IN THIS ORDER, AND THE ORDER IS REASONED. (1) REF-01002 backward -- the highest-value target on the slug by its own framing, a 2009 study saying design recommendations for either the running slope or the cross slope requirements are based on limited empirical research, so it cites whatever empirical work existed. BLOCKED BEHIND GAP-016: no DOI, therefore no Crossref deposit, so its reference list can only come from the article, which GAP-016 must obtain anyway to settle C10. Reading it discharges both. (2) REF-00979 backward -- ranks second on the GAP-018 predictor (a paper cites the literature of its own independent variable; Chow et al. measure propulsion across a slope series), and mining it is therefore also a PROSPECTIVE TEST of that predictor, with the prediction already recorded in its deferral note before the pass. (3) REF-00980 backward -- a 1997 paper cites pre-1997 work, and the pre-1997 ramp-slope literature is exactly what REF-01002 abstract calls limited; expected yield modest, stated in advance. (4) REF-00983 and REF-00986 backward -- batch 08 deferrals, the oldest in the register, and REF-00986 own extraction is graded absent so its references are unlikely to be gradient-bearing; both cheap. (5) REF-00999, REF-01000, REF-01001 backward -- T3, so R2 depth-2-3 obligation over CONFIRMED T1-T2 anchors reaches them only secondarily; take them only if capacity remains. (6) REF-00989 and REF-00993 FORWARD -- both Japanese-language, no DOI, absent from every citation index, so the forward graph does not reach them. THESE TWO ARE NOT A MINING PASS AND MUST NOT BE DRESSED AS ONE: the tractable equivalent is a Japanese-language site search for organisations quoting the same framing, which is a SEARCH and is recorded as owed. WHAT DISCHARGE REQUIRES: a pass that runs clears its deferral only with --discharge-deferral, which asserts the standing deferral belongs to the direction just run; without it the deferral stands and log-mining prints deferral_still_standing. Batch 17 closes this gap by emptying the backlog or by re-deferring with fresh reasons -- never by silence.

abstract present: True
<jats:p>A ramp is the basic type of an assisting device for wheelchair users. Although the height of a ramp is an important design element, it has not been considered in prior studies. Therefore, in this study, the ramp slope and height are considered as independent variables. To analyze the effects of the slope and height, five levels of slope (1:6, 1:8, 1:10, 1:12 and 1:14) and three levels of height (15 cm, 30 cm and 45 cm) are considered. For the dependent variables, the total time and velocity were considered as performance measures, pulse rate changes and EMG signals of four related muscles (extensor carpi radialis, triceps brachii, anterior deltoid and posterior deltoid) were considered as physiology measures, and perceived discomfort while ascending and descending were considered as perceived discomfort measures. As a result, differences among performance, physiological characteristic and perceived discomfort for the five slopes increased as the height increased. Additionally, slope effects were minor when the height was low (15 cm). In summary, there was no significant difference between 1:10 and 1:12 (as suggested by ADAAG). In addition, slope effects were minor at a low height; thus, a slope of 1:8 can be recommended if the installation space for a gentler ramp is not sufficient.</jats:p>

=== notation family for ratio ===
#: its own ACTION (4): composing across THEM stays refused. Adding a member here is
#: a claim that two notations denote the same quantity exactly, which is a
#: mathematical claim and should be made deliberately.
NOTATION_FAMILIES = {
    "gradient": ("%", "rise:run ratio"),
}
#: Every family member MUST appear here, and the guard below refuses one that does
#: not. Without it, adding a notation to the tuple above and forgetting the
#: arithmetic makes `to_canonical` fall through to `Fraction(text)` and read the
#: number AS IF it were already canonical -- `5` degrees silently becoming `5 %`.
#: That is the shape a reviewer of the 2026-09-17 ruling flagged: `degrees` is the
#: ARCTANGENT of the ratio, not a rescaling of it, so it is not a notation of this
#: quantity at all and belongs to a family of its own or to none. Membership is a
#: mathematical claim; this makes forgetting to back it up an error rather than a
#: wrong answer.
_CONVERTIBLE = {"%", "rise:run ratio"}
_RATIO_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*:\s*(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*$")


def notation_family(unit):
    """Which family a stated unit belongs to, or None if it stands alone."""
    for fam, members in NOTATION_FAMILIES.items():
        if (unit or "").strip() in members:
            return fam
    return None


def to_canonical(raw, unit):
    """One stated value -> an exact Fraction on its family's canonical scale.

    The canonical scale is the family's FIRST member -- percent for gradient -- and
    the conversion is exact because it is done in Fraction, never float: `1:12` is
    100/12, which is 8.333... and is never rounded here. Rounding happens once, at
    render, and is marked inexact when it happens.

All figures below were re-derived; commands are given beside them. Ranked worst first.

---

**1. The determination chain's "operative reason" is which index holds the record, not whether the paper was read — and the batch admitted two sources on the exact evidential basis it says disqualifies the third.**
Artifact: `/home/user/guidebook/sessions/session_2026-09-18-research-batch-17-vredenburgh-full-read-and-mining.md:26-28, 192-193`; GAP-026 (DB row).
Claim: "REF-01002 stays `UNVERIFIED`, determination gate 1 stays open, C10 keeps refusing the re-determination … the cell stays undetermined because C10 blocks on REF-01002, unread."
Why it does not follow: REF-01003 and REF-01004 were written `verification_status=VERIFIED, verification_method='tool', verified_by_tool='crossref'` while their own extraction rows say "extraction_method SKIM on a deposited abstract; the full text is not read" (extraction 51 notes). The manifest shows only Crossref API JSON was fetched for both — metadata plus abstract, the same thing TRID returned for REF-01002, which batch 16 demoted to UNVERIFIED because "VERIFIED is reachable only by a method that OBTAINS THE ARTEFACT". I4's allow-list (`test_db_integrity.py:379-383`) admits `'tool'` as artefact-obtaining; Crossref does not return the artefact. So the "second anchoring-tier stated value" (REF-01004) would pass C10 and REF-01002 would fail it, on identical read-ness — the distinguishing fact is DOI existence. Further: no re-determination was attempted this batch (the only `assess_cell.py` invocation in the command log is `--help`), so "C10 keeps refusing" describes a test that was never run. C10 is a post-hoc count over `specifications` (`test_db_integrity.py:558-566`); the engine itself does not exclude UNVERIFIED sources from anchoring (`_is_disqualified`, `assess_cell.py:187-197`, D-0157: "a plain UNVERIFIED source is NOT disqualified"), so run today it would EMIT a provisional cell governed by `[REF-01002, REF-01004]` and the blocking test would go red afterwards. That is an engine/test contradiction (D-0157 vs C10) narrated as a mechanical refusal.
Commands:
`python3 -c "import sqlite3;c=sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True);print(c.execute(\"select ref_id,verification_status,verification_method,verified_by_tool from evidence_sources where ref_id in ('REF-01002','REF-01003','REF-01004')\").fetchall())"` → REF-01002 UNVERIFIED/corroborated-not-retrieved; 01003/01004 VERIFIED/tool/crossref.

**2. "The GAP-018 predictor is FALSIFIED" and "the strict screen inverts the original ranking" rest on (a) a top-ranked anchor that was never re-derived, (b) two different screens presented as one series, and (c) predictions registered against one instrument and scored against another.**
Artifact: session record §2 (lines 35-67); GAP-029 (DB); `data_20260918213944_*.sql:36`.
Claims: "Both failed, in opposite directions. That is the hypothesis being wrong, not noise." / "REF-00980: 5 → 4 of 25 — the anchor I predicted low survives best… The strict screen inverts the original ranking." / "Every mining yield this project has recorded used the loose screen."
Why it does not follow:
(a) REF-00985 — the anchor that founded GAP-018 at 23/46 — was "(not re-fetched this batch)" in the batch's own strict-screen script, though its payload sits in `retrieval-log/session_2026-09-18-research-batch-16-backward-mining-t2-anchors/4062c068e5f7280f.json`. Under the batch's own STRICT regex it scores **8/46**, the highest absolute count of any anchor, and REF-00984 stays 0/38. The founding observation survives the strict screen; the ranking is not inverted; the anchor "surviving best" is the one the batch did not look at.
(b) Batch 16's screen was a 24-term regex (`…|barrier|built environment|wayfinding|negotiat|ascent|…`); batch 17's LOOSE is 15 terms. GAP-027's "RUNNING TALLY" (23/46, 19/30, 6/117, 5/25, 0/38) mixes both; under batch-17 LOOSE REF-00977 is 5/117 not 6/117. The pre-registered floor ≥8 was calibrated on batch-16's wider screen and scored on a narrower one — never like-for-like.
(c) Under STRICT, REF-00986 = 0/45 which PASSES its ≤4 ceiling; the §2 table's ✗ marks sit only in the loose column. "Both failed" is true only under the instrument the same section declares confounded. Swapping the instrument after seeing results and then declaring the hypothesis falsified is the post-hoc move DR-2026-05-09 forbids for priors, applied to the dependent variable.
(d) STRICT lacks `uphill`; REF-00979 ref [10] "level and uphill wheelchair propulsion" is a slope paper it misses. "2 of 30" is an artefact of the second regex; a hand count is 3/30. The retraction replaced one unvalidated instrument's output with another's and called it "the honest figure".
